page: Microsoft Azure D16a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.35 GHz, allocating 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 429 GB of local SSD temporary storage and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable general-purpose compute capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached a strong top-25% result of 2707.27, while multi-core performance scored 21649.45. Geekbench evaluations yielded scores of 1394.0 in single-core and 8187.0 in multi-core tasks, alongside balanced scores across software compilation (13244.0) and ray tracing (16050.0). Small model (135M) LLM text generation achieved a strong 276.2 tokens per second, while 7B model generation measured 14.03 tokens per second.

The primary architectural constraint lies in memory write throughput. While cached read bandwidth is substantial at 799.89 GB/sec, uncached large-block write operations scored 25.81 GB/sec, falling into the bottom 25% tier. Additionally, vector instructions are limited to standard AVX, lacking AVX-512 extensions. The server is well suited for balanced enterprise workloads such as relational databases, web application hosting, build systems, and general business applications that benefit from integrated local SSD scratch space.
